subject: NimbusCare: unexpected access-squeeze impacting latency & error rate
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbuscare.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency and 429 spike — immediate assistance requested

Kimberly,

We started seeing a huge increase in end-user latency and a rise in 429s hitting our API consumers starting around 07:50 PDT. Response times went from ~120ms to 1.2s and some endpoints are returning 429s for sustained bursts. Our product team is fielding customer complaints. I've attached a short log extract that shows repeated retries from a handful of client IPs and a cluster of 429s tied to the same tenant token.

Can you route this to the on-call or engineering lead? We need something we can communicate to customers in the next 30–45 minutes.

Attachment: nimbuscare_429s_snippet.txt (text, 34 lines)

Thanks,
Elena
CTO, NimbusCare
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-21T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency and 429 spike — immediate assistance requested

Team — forwarding NimbusCare. Symptoms: sudden latency increase and clustered 429s. Elena included a log extract (attached). Immediate asks: (1) triage root cause (rate/quota/burst config?) (2) a safe mitigation we can apply (short rollback/parameter tweak) and (3) a customer-facing one-paragraph that my AM can send to their execs.

Quick context: NimbusCare is on Dedicated tier with custom quota windows (deal NC-4372). Their traffic pattern has big momentary fanouts from a third-party integration. Suspect burst window or token-bucket leak.

Please @Connor for triage. Monica, please standby for comms. Marissa, heads-up if exec escalation needed.

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-21T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency and 429 spike — immediate assistance requested

I'm looking at the trace and metrics now. Initial findings:
- The tenant-level burst bucket is configured with a long decay (burst_reset_interval = 600s) while the inbound pacing window is 60s. That mismatch means sustained microbursts can drain the bucket and keep it in a suppressed state for many minutes.
- We see a retry loop pattern from a handful of client IPs (exponential backoff not applied). The retries are short enough to register as a continuous burst against the tenant.
- The safety valve we normally trigger (regional fallback) didn't engage because the request attribution still mapped to the same tenant token; routing is fine.

Immediate mitigation options (risk/benefit):
1) Short term: temporarily reduce burst_reset_interval to 30s for the tenant -> will allow the bucket to recover faster. Low risk, quick revert.
2) Medium term: add a short-lived override to increase per-second capacity (emergency uplift) for 15 minutes and enable request-sampling guardrails to identify offending IPs. Higher risk to unit economics, but minimizes customer impact.
3) Long term: recommend aligning burst_reset_interval with pacing window and add a retry-adaptive ingress filter to damp obvious retry loops.

I'll prepare the CLI commands and a safe rollback. Kimberly — if we have permission, I'll apply option 1 immediately. Also capturing metrics snapshot and a playbook note.

--
Connor O'Brien
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency and 429 spike — immediate assistance requested

Elena — thank you for the quick heads-up and the log snippet. Connor confirms the likely cause is a misaligned burst policy combined with heavy client retries. Proposed immediate plan: (a) apply a temporary burst reset reduction (600s -> 30s) for 15 minutes, (b) enable emergency per-second uplift if needed, (c) run a short IP-scan to identify repeat offenders and share back a list.

Requesting your permission to apply the short-term change (plan A). We'll watch latency and 429 rate and revert if any negative side-effects appear. Attached: playbook_emergency_adjustment.md and a live metrics snapshot.

If you prefer a different approach, tell me now — otherwise we'll proceed on your go-ahead.

Attachment: playbook_emergency_adjustment.md (markdown, 1.2kB)
Attachment: metrics_snapshot_2029-05-21.png (image, 140kB)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note & customer relief offer

Kim / Connor — please proceed with the lowest-risk mitigation. Also, a few exec-level asks:
- Prep a one-paragraph public statement we can share with NimbusCare execs summarizing cause and remediation steps (Kim will send).
- Assess SLA credit exposure for a ~30–45m elevated error/latency window; I expect the finance team will request an estimate.
- If mitigation fails, prepare a hotfix to allow temporary dedicated capacity burst (we can authorize up to 2x for 30 minutes).

I'll join a call if you need leadership presence. Keep me posted every 20 minutes.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbuscare.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nimbuscare.com
Date: 2029-05-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Latency and 429 spike — immediate assistance requested

Kim — please proceed with plan A. We appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll pause the integration causing the fanout and follow up after you confirm metrics.

Also: please include a short note we can send to our execs describing root cause and next steps (one paragraph). We'll need the timeline for when the bucket mismatch will be permanently fixed.

Thanks again — Elena
